summary.headline: Finkurve's Q2 FY27 AUM grew about 95% YoY but only about 3% QoQ, with GNPA rising to about 2.6% and collection efficiency falling to about 90%.
summary.overview: Management said Q2 FY27 was among its best quarters on operating profit, up 62% YoY, with AUM up about 95% YoY and branches up to 122 from 92 a year earlier. Growth slowed sharply sequentially, which management attributed to the revised RBI gold loan framework, deferred borrowing after gold price correction, and competition. Asset quality weakened: GNPA rose to about 2.6% and NNPA was 2.4%, with collection efficiency down to about 90% from about 98% in Q1, which management called a technical classification rather than a credit cost issue. Co-lending rose to about 6% of AUM, and management reiterated a target of 30-35% off-book AUM within about three years.

financial_highlights.change: QoQ slowed from about 16% in Q1 and over 30% in Q4 (as stated by analyst)

financial_highlights.value: Highest quarterly operational profit reported (figure not stated)

financial_highlights.change: First time in a couple of quarters, with leverage above 2.5x
From 92 a year earlier; 4 added in Q2 vs 13 in Q1
No fresh NCDs raised in Q2

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Core business, about 90% of the portfolio mix as stated by management; yield rose to 20.8% from 20%. Branches are concentrated in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

segments.name: Personal loans (partnership-led, via digital lending apps/LSPs)
segments.commentary: About 4% of AUM and about 27% of interest income per analyst; average ticket about Rs 20,000, tenure 15 days to 6-9 months; portfolio averaged Rs 45-50 crore QoQ. Management said net economics to Finkurve are a hurdle rate, with excess yield passed to partners.

segments.name: Co-lending / off-book
segments.commentary: Off-book AUM roughly doubled to about Rs 78 crore in Q2; the entire sequential AUM growth was passed to co-lending partners. Two partners live, a third to go live in Q3 and a revived partner in Q4.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 50-60% for FY27; management sees no concern in reaching it, with updates to come if needed.
Branch expansion: about 150 branches by December 2026 (adding about 28), and 60-70 branches for FY27, versus the 50-60 branch guidance mentioned in the Q&A.
Off-book AUM target of 30-35% of overall book within about 3 years, described as mid to long term.
Personal loan AUM target of about Rs 150 crore by end of FY27.
Bank borrowings to rise; NCDs capped at 40-45% of total borrowings; several bank sanctions already received.
Expect average ticket size to fall further as the company consciously shifts to smaller tickets.
capex_capacity: Branches: 122 at 30 Sep 2026; management expects about 150 by December 2026 and 60-70 additions for FY27, with the second half seen as faster.
Cash flow-based (income-generating) lending is at a very small share; staff training and system changes are in progress, and management said this would take time.
Augmont brand transition under way for the gold loan business to create a single customer-facing brand.
Appointed a Chief Compliance Officer and continued investment in risk, technology, operations and governance.
demand_pricing: Gold price correction from earlier-2026 highs deferred customer borrowing: customers realise less per loan amount, so they wait a quarter for prices to stabilise.
Renewals were 60-65% when gold prices were high, now about 10-15%; customer retention at maturity above 60% (as stated).
Competition from banks and larger gold NBFCs is rising; management said its edge is turnaround time, scheme design and access to under-banked customers in Tier 2/3 markets, not product.

LTV rose, which management attributed to the RBI 85% LTV allowance for consumption loans, a small income-generating book kept at up to 85%, and price correction; management said accrued interest is included in LTV.
Ticket size falling due to the slab-wise LTV regime; management said it lacked data on the split and will share it after the call.
Unorganised lenders' share is falling (management cited a 60:40 to 65:35 shift) as RBI restricted repledging.

Augmont has more than 350 standard products distributed by gold loan companies, and one gold loan company sold over 28 tonnes of Augmont jewellery; Finkurve has only just started this non-interest income line.

qa_highlights.question: How will Finkurve differentiate from banks and large gold NBFCs as banks get aggressive on gold loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no product differentiation; it targets customers with little access to banks or large NBFCs, and turnaround times and scheme design are key. Yields are higher because of this segment.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue rose about 20% QoQ while AUM grew only 3%; what drove the gap, and was any of it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to gold loan yield rising to 20.8% from 20% and co-lending share rising to about 5.8% from 1-2%. Management said there was no one-off income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did GNPA rise and how much will be recovered through auctions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to the shift from bullet repayment to monthly or quarterly repayment under the new framework, and said most accounts have since regularised. Auction is a last resort; the CFO said NPAs are a technical classification, with margin still sufficient to recover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did collection efficiency fall to about 90% from about 98%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the decline in collection efficiency raised delinquencies and the NPA ratio. He said NPA levels are on par with the industry average at steady gold prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AUM growth slow to about 3% QoQ, and what is guided for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a transition, not a slowdown. Drivers were the regulatory framework, deferred borrowing after gold price correction, and competition. Guidance of 50-60% AUM growth for FY27 stands.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the average ticket size falling, and how much is due to slab-wise LTV rules? What are renewal and top-up shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is a conscious move to smaller tickets, partly driven by LTV schemes; the split was not available on the call. Renewals fell to about 10-15% from 60-65%; retention at maturity is above 60%. Precise data to follow by email.

qa_highlights.question: What is the on-book/off-book AUM split and the personal loan economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-book share rose to about 6% from 1-3%, with the entire sequential AUM growth passed to co-lending partners. Personal loans are partnership-led, with a hurdle-rate model; average ticket about Rs 20,000.

risks_watch: Asset quality: GNPA about 2.6%, collection efficiency about 90%, and NPAs driven by the move from bullet to periodic repayment; watch the Q3 GNPA trend and how fast accounts regularise.
Growth momentum: QoQ AUM growth of about 3% against 50-60% annual guidance requires a sharp pickup in H2.
Gold price volatility affecting renewals, ticket sizes and borrower demand.
Funding cost and mix: NCDs at about 57% of borrowings with a 40-45% cap; bank and co-lending partner onboarding timing is key.
Regulatory shift to cash flow-based lending: management said staff capability is limited, so the share and pricing of such loans are unproven.
Stock performance: the individual investor asked why shares have not re-rated despite growth; management declined to comment on the share price.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term franchise and guidance, but defensive on asset quality and the sequential slowdown, which it reframed as industry transition. Evasive on share price and on several data requests (ticket size split, renewals, LTV data), promised to share later.
